decision_table.name: Determine_SC_Filing_Requirement
decision_table.description: Determine if corporation must file South Carolina state corporate tax return. Checks for physical presence or economic nexus.

condition.name: has_physical_presence
condition.comment: Has physical presence in SC (office, employees, property)

actions.action: // Physical nexus established - filing required // Apportionment will be calculated by tables 7000-7500

rule.policy:
SC filing required due to physical presence (office, employees, or property in state).
A corporation has physical presence nexus in SC if it has: - An office, store, warehouse, or other place of business in SC - Employees working in SC - Tangible personal property located in SC - Real property located in SC
Reference: SC Code § 12-6-2320 (Nexus and apportionment) Reference: SC Department of Revenue Regulation 117-1730 (Nexus standards)

actions.action: // Economic nexus established per Wayfair - filing required // Apportionment will be calculated by tables 7000-7500

rule.policy:
SC filing required due to economic nexus (post-Wayfair).
Economic nexus threshold: $100,000 gross receipts OR 200 transactions in SC.
Following South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc., 138 S. Ct. 2080 (2018), SC requires filing if a corporation exceeds economic nexus thresholds, even without physical presence.
Reference: South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc., 138 S. Ct. 2080 (2018) Reference: SC Department of Revenue Economic Nexus Guidance Reference: SC Code § 12-36-2691 (Economic nexus provisions)

No SC nexus - no filing requirement.
Corporation does not meet physical presence or economic nexus thresholds. Any estimated payments would be refunded.
Reference: SC Code § 12-6-2320 (Nexus requirements)

decision_table.name: Calculate_SC_Income_Adjustments
decision_table.description: Calculate SC state-specific additions and subtractions to federal taxable income.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to calculate adjustments

rule.policy:
SC state-specific income adjustments to federal taxable income.
SC ADDITIONS to federal taxable income include: - Interest income from U.S. government obligations (exempt federally, taxable to SC) - IRC Section 199A qualified business income deduction addback (SC does not conform) - State income tax refunds included in federal income - Bonus depreciation addback (varies by tax year) - Expenses related to exempt income
SC SUBTRACTIONS from federal taxable income include: - Interest on SC state and municipal bonds - SC net operating loss deduction (subject to SC limitations) - Dividend income eligible for SC dividend received deduction - Certain capital gains exclusions
Reference: SC Form SC1120 Schedule A (Adjustments to Federal Taxable Income) Reference: SC Code § 12-6-1130 (Additions to federal taxable income) Reference: SC Code § 12-6-1140 (Deductions from federal taxable income)

No nexus - no state adjustments calculated.
Corporation does not have SC nexus, so no income adjustments are needed.

decision_table.name: Calculate_SC_State_Tax
decision_table.description: Calculate SC state corporate income tax. Applies SC 5% flat rate to apportioned and adjusted taxable income. Also includes SC annual license fee.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to owe tax

rule.policy:
SC state corporate income tax calculation:
1. Federal taxable income: [Form 1120 line 28] 2. Apportioned to SC: × [SC apportionment percentage] 3. SC additions: + [Federal interest, IRC 199A addback, etc.] 4. SC subtractions: - [SC municipal interest, SC NOL, etc.] 5. SC taxable income: = [Result] 6. SC tax rate: × 5.0% (flat rate) 7. SC income tax: = [Tax before credits] 8. SC credits: - [Job development, corporate HQ, port volume, R&D, etc.] 9. SC license fee: + [0.1% of capital and paid-in surplus, minimum $15] 10. SC tax liability: = [Final tax]
SC uses single-sales factor apportionment (100% sales factor).
SC tax rate history: - 2025: 5.0% flat rate - Historical: 5.0% flat rate (stable)
SC provides various tax credits including: - Job development credit - Corporate headquarters credit - Port volume increase credit - Research and development credit - Manufacturing and recycling credit - Renewable energy credit
SC annual license fee: - Rate: 0.1% of capital stock and paid-in surplus - Minimum: $15 - Due with corporate income tax return
Reference: SC Form SC1120 (Corporation Income Tax Return) Reference: SC Code § 12-6-530 (Tax rate of 5%) Reference: SC Code § 12-6-2320 (Single-sales apportionment) Reference: SC Code § 12-20-50 (License fee) Reference: SC Department of Revenue Corporate Tax Guide

No SC nexus - no tax liability.
Corporation does not have physical presence or economic nexus in SC. Any estimated payments are refunded.
Reference: SC Code § 12-6-2320 (Nexus requirements)

No SC taxable income - only license fee applies.
Corporation has SC nexus but no positive taxable income after apportionment and adjustments. However, SC annual license fee ($15 minimum) still applies.
SC net operating loss (NOL) rules may apply: - SC allows NOL carryforward for 15 years - No carryback allowed (as of 2025) - NOL limited to 80% of taxable income (similar to federal)
Reference: SC Form SC1120 (Corporation Income Tax Return) Reference: SC Code § 12-6-1500 (Net operating loss deduction) Reference: SC Code § 12-20-50 (License fee requirement)
